extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational journalism, NLP, and social media analysis studying clickbait detection and media behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, and applying automated methods to identify clickbait headlines in news/video posts (especially on Facebook) and analyzing their topical distribution, prevalence across media categories, and engagement effects. Includes dataset construction, embedding/model choices, topic modeling for short texts, and impact analysis using social metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait identification (binary classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define clickbait identification as a supervised binary classification problem with class set C = {clickbait, non clickbait}, mapping sentences/headlines to one of these labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally: given X (sentences) and labeled training set S ⊂ X×C, learn γ: X → C. Use labeled headline data to train and evaluate classifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data labeling standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use manually labeled headlines where each headline is labeled as clickbait or non-clickbait by at least three volunteers (example: the Headlines dataset with 32,000 labeled headlines: 15,999 clickbait, 16,001 non-clickbait).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer multiple annotators per item to reduce noise and report dataset class counts; do not assume whole sites are entirely clickbait or non-clickbait (avoid site-level labeling bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature representation: distributed subword embeddings (Skip-Gramsw)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a Skip-Gramsw model that incorporates subword (substring) information to learn vector representations for words; a word embedding is formed by summing the vector representations of its subwords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skip-Gramsw helps share representations across words and improves representations for rare words; see example of subwords {qui, uic, ick} for 'quick'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trained vs domain-specific embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare and use pre-trained vectors (e.g., Google News word2vec) and vectors learned from an in-domain Media Corpus (headlines, messages, bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with combinations (pre-trained on headlines only, headlines+messages, headlines+bodies+messages). Domain-specific embeddings can outperform huge general corpora for the clickbait task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding dimensionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 300-dimensional word embeddings when learning vectors for this task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set embedding size to 300 as in experiments; be consistent when comparing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence representation: averaging word embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a sentence/headline representation by averaging the embeddings of the words present in the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the averaged vector as the hidden representation input to a classifier (simple and effective baseline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifier architecture: linear softmax
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a linear classifier with a softmax output over the classes to compute probability distribution for clickbait vs non-clickbait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep classifier simple when using strong distributed representations; compare against other learners as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol: cross-validation and repeated runs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models using 10-fold cross-validation and repeat each experiment multiple times (example: 5 runs) to avoid randomness effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report averages across runs for stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report accuracy, precision, recall, F-measure (F1), area under the ROC curve (ROC-AUC), and Cohen’s κ for classifier performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all metrics (not just accuracy) because class distributions and agreement measures matter; especially relevant when overall accuracy is already high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline methods and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare proposed methods against baselines such as bag-of-words (BOW) with hand-crafted features and published prior systems (e.g., Chakraborty et al., Anand et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight improvements (e.g., Skip-Gramsw outperforms BOW and previous works) and note dataset/version differences that can affect comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of short-text topic modeling (Biterm Topic Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: For topic analysis of short texts like headlines, use Biterm Topic Modeling (BTM) which models aggregated word-word co-occurrence patterns rather than document-level co-occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: LDA/LSA may struggle with sparsity in short documents; represent topics as ordered lists of top words and compare clickbait vs non-clickbait topic distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-body similarity measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure similarity between the headline and the article 'intro' (first paragraph) as a proxy for how well the headline represents the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bag-of-words vectors and cosine similarity between headline and sentences in the first paragraph; note limitation and plan to replace with embedding-based similarity in future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption: first paragraph represents article summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the first paragraph of a news article represents the summary of the whole article (used for headline-body similarity computation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite journalism fundamentals and acknowledge this is an approximation; consider alternatives for different news styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement/impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Facebook reactions (Like, Love, Haha, Wow, Sad, Angry), comments, and shares as metrics of user engagement and reachability for posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate reactions as a single sum where useful; compare average engagement per clickbait vs non-clickbait post across media categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prevalence metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute percentage of clickbait headlines per media organization and per media category (e.g., mainstream vs unreliable; broadcast vs print; subcategories like satire, conspiracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use kernel density estimation and per-category summaries to reveal distributional differences (e.g., broadcast non-news vs news broadcast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reposting frequency analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze how often the same link/article is reposted by media on Facebook by counting repost occurrences per link (example threshold: consider links reposted at least 20 times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare reposting behavior across media categories to identify repetitive posting patterns (noting that conspiracy media may repeat links more).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait use in status messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the presence of clickbait-style language in Facebook status messages even when the linked article is non-clickbait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute percentage of non-clickbait links accompanied by clickbait status messages for each media category to capture promotional practices beyond headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus selection and filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect a large media corpus (example: 1.67 million Facebook posts from 153 U.S.-based media organizations, 2014–2016) and limit to specific post types (link and video) for headline/title extraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document selection criteria (which outlets included, category cross-checking, period) and filter by post types; collect accompanying bodies where available (e.g., for 191,540 link posts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model limitation and future criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the limitation that current models consider only the headline when deciding clickbaitiness and propose incorporating headline-body similarity as part of the clickbait definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to systematically incorporate content similarity into the model so that headlines that fairly represent bodies are not labeled clickbait despite sensational wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and data release
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare to make collected corpora and pre-trained domain embeddings publicly available for research upon acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document dataset URLs, preprocessing steps, and embedding training settings to enable replication and further study.
